What a completion does is one table read in the step (COMPLETION_EFFECTS, projects.mjs:1113-1433): every row answers before anything is written, an `apply` that throws is caught and told to the GMs, a removal can be kept for the completing character's Reroll (`keep`), and a refused stretch offers the target again (heldForRepick / offerRepick 1454-1472).

A secret project carries no name and no told-apart ownership in the Countdowns every browser holds (HIDDEN_NAME, ownershipMap: projects-secrecy.mjs:128, 370-382); its name, viewers, room, murder mark, description and room action are the GMs' (PROJECT_SECRET_FIELDS 111-113, PROJECT_SECRET_WHILE_SECRET 224), and setProjectMeta moves the while-secret fields across when the secrecy changes (282-307).

An insider's sight is a client-setting copy the primary sends addressed and the player asks for at every load, so a cleared chat log no longer takes a secret project, its words or its room action out of an insider's tray (projects.mjs:441-468, 495-608).

A description too long is refused on every road, never cut: createProject, updateProject and cleanProjectChange, the last reaching another GM's project.change and a console's applyProjectChange (projects.mjs:1496-1508, 2061-2064, 2594-2597).

The sabotage pair is taken back only as written: unsabotageRefusal is pure and ties the undo to the repair that froze the target and to the saboteur who asked (projects.mjs:2329-2337); a repair is made and its target frozen in one step, which refuses a gone, frozen or repair target (createInStep 1878-1886).

What only the roller saw of a Work or a Sabotage - tool relief, concealment bonus or penalty - is held to the rules by one pair of readers on the GM, against the tools as the GMs hold them (action-project.mjs:680-704).

A watched sabotage of a secret project or an indirect murder names no project to the room (sabotageWatchedLine, action-project.mjs:1256-1263); a failed concealment of an indirect murder is told to the room in a sentence that names no project (737-744).

What a player saw last is kept on that player's own browser, written only when one of their characters stands in the room; another player's move costs a bystander nothing (projects-seen.mjs:378-385), and a repair is known only from a visit that listed it (asSeen 172-176).

A Daggerheart countdown keeps its direction at the module's first write to it (projects-secrecy.mjs:275-281), and a GM's tray -/+ on a project row is one change of the entry (projects-ui.mjs:201-215).

Project tokens carry a neutral name, are found by their own flag, orphans are removed and duplicates only warned of, and the module's own moves and deletions are marked so a GM's drag or Delete is read as a choice (projects-map.mjs:79-100, 386-494, 656-722).
Every literal DRPG.* key the seven files use has an English and a Polish twin (265 checked by script, and the prefix families).

findings.title: A GM running a student's Work on Project or Sabotage acts as the GM's account: every secret project in the room is offered, and the Work is filed as the GM's own change, not that student's work
findings.where: scripts/action-project.mjs:66, 108, 474 and 1165 (the lists built with the default user); scripts/projects.mjs:938-941, 954-956, 968-990 (`user = game.user`); scripts/projects.mjs:1036-1037 (kind "gm" when the mover is this GM), 1067, 1592 (noteProjectWork only for player, call, reroll); scripts/bridge-runs-records.mjs:45 (a non-primary GM's progress filed "gm")
findings.what_happens: performProject, workOnProject and performSabotage build their lists with projectsAvailableIn(place), projectsListedIn(place) and sabotageTargetsIn(place, { anyRoom }), whose `user` defaults to game.user. On a GM's browser canSee answers true for every project, so a GM who plays an absent player's student - the flow sabotageTargets' own comment names as supported ('to play an absent player's character', action-project.mjs:1149-1158) - is offered every secret project standing in that room, another player's indirect murder among them, preselected when it is the first workable row (projectOptionsHtml 833-845). The progress then goes through addProgress with no `by` and no `kind`, which files it as kind "gm" (projects.mjs:1036-1037), and applyProjectChange notes a student's work this time of day only for player, call and reroll (1592): the Monocub's Tinker rule (E72 C13, DC23/DC24, 'only while a living student worked on it this time of day') does not count that student's Work. The bridge holds a player's request to the sender (bridge-guards.mjs:718-724) - this is only the GM's own road.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM plays absent Bea's student in the Kitchen, opens Work on Project and presses Roll on the default row: progress lands on Aiko's secret poison trap, which Bea's student cannot know exists, and later a Monocub's Tinker is refused there because no student worked on it this time of day.
findings.expected: The lists of a student's action read the character's players (as the bridge reads the sender: projectsAvailableIn(place, owner)), and a GM's Work on a student's behalf counts as that student's work.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a narrowing to the character's owner on the GM's road: none in performProject, workOnProject, performSabotage, chooseProject or projectOptionsHtml; room-tile.mjs:146 says outright that 'a GM sees the secret ones' for its own count, which is the GM's view, not a student's. The bridge's projectWithinReach (bridge-guards.mjs:718-724) passes `sender`, but a GM's own client never goes through it (addProgress writes directly on a GM, projects.mjs:1007, 1036). No test of a GM-run student's Work list was found (grep of the tier files for projectsAvailableIn with a GM reader).

findings.title: A new target on a countdown that counts down (one made in Daggerheart's own window) keeps what was left, not what was done: raising it adds progress, lowering it takes progress away
findings.where: scripts/projects.mjs:1773-1774 (the clamp in changeStep), 2609-2611 (projectEditChange's note), 807 (allProjects reads progress as start - current); reached from the project window's Save (projects-ui.mjs:1229-1255) and the manager, which list every countdown
findings.what_happens: For a countdown with countsUp false, allProjects reads progress done as `start - raw`. A change of target writes `{ start: target, current: Math.min(raw, target) }` for both directions, so `raw` - what is left - is kept and progress done becomes `target - raw`. A Daggerheart countdown of 8 with 6 done (raw 2) raised to 10 reads 8 done; lowered to 4 it reads 2 done (min(2, 4) = 2 left), not finished. A module project (countsUp true) is right, `current` being progress earned. The comment says the clamp is right for both directions because what is left 'cannot exceed the start either' - true, but the progress achieved is not preserved, which is what the window's 'Scale' change means.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM opens a countdown an adversary feature made, 6 of 8 done, and changes its Scale to Desperate (8 -> 10) in the module's window: the tray now reads 8 of 10, two points nobody earned.
findings.expected: For a countdown that counts down, keep progress done: current = clamp(newTarget - (oldStart - raw), 0, newTarget).
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that such a countdown reaches the step with up = false: changeStep reads countsUp before its own meta write (projects.mjs:1669, 1814) and setProjectMeta stamps countsUp false on the first write of a countdown with no row (projects-secrecy.mjs:281), so `up` is false throughout. Checked the edit window offers the target for it: openProjectManager lists allProjects, every countdown (projects-ui.mjs:689), and Edit opens openProjectDialog with the scale select (957-1114). No tier test of a target change on a down-counting countdown was found (grep of 'what is LEFT', 'Math.min(raw' in the tier files). AUDIT-1.2.13 A15 (line 563) was the identical ternary, made one line, not this arithmetic.

Clear Chat Log (or the card deleted) removes it; the GMs' row carries proposerTold, so tellProposers at the next load posts nothing again. The proposer is then known only by the room rule. The case the road was written for (H84-04: a proposer the GM placed in a room, or whose room the approval changed, who never stood there) loses the project from tray, token and asSeen. The comment at 335-336 says a card's words reach a browser that was away when a GM gives them again (secret.mjs askForWords) - that is for a card that still exists, not one deleted.

findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another reader of the proposer on a player's browser: proposedBy is the only one, and sealedViewers is written only by a reveal (projects-secrecy.mjs:538). Looked for a resend: tellProposers skips every row with proposerTold (683); retellSights resends sights only (540-545). Scenario 66 E4 reads the card on p1 (66-rooms.mjs:381-401) but clears no chat; scenario 72's cleared-log phase is about sights and descriptions. findings.title: Show on the map pressed by a GM who is not the primary writes projectMeta whole and places the token on that GM's browser, outside the primary's queue
findings.where: scripts/projects-map.mjs:746-753 (showProjectOnMap), 68-70 (writeTokenRecord: a step of COUNTDOWNS_KEY on this browser), 592-599 (syncProjectToken: isGM only, its own per-project queue on this browser); scripts/projects-ui.mjs:598-605 (the manager's button, any GM); projects-secrecy.mjs:308-314 (setProjectMeta writes the setting whole)
findings.what_happens: Every other road to a project's token runs on the primary: a change's sync after its step (projects.mjs:1611-1617), the scene draw's syncProjectTokens (projects-map.mjs:789), the drag and the deletion hooks (657, 710). showProjectOnMap asks only game.user.isGM: on a second GM it writes { mapHidden: false } through setProjectMeta, which reads projectMeta and writes it whole, in a queue only that browser orders, then runs syncProjectToken there, which places the token and writes tokenId and tokenScene the same way. The E36 fix e1-G5 note above writeTokenRecord records the loss this queue was made to stop (E36-T10: a step's projectMeta write and a token record putting back each other's copy) - ordered on one browser, it does not order a write against the primary's steps, and syncProjectToken's per-project queue does not order it against a primary sync of the same project.
findings.failure_scenario: A second GM presses Show on the map while the primary's step writes a room change of another project: one of the two projectMeta writes lands over the other, and the other project's room, or this one's token record, is lost.
findings.expected: Show on the map is one change of the entry on the primary (a meta change of mapHidden, whose sync then runs on the primary), as createProject's placing was moved there in E36 C4.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a primary gate in showProjectOnMap, syncProjectToken and placeProjectToken: none (isGM only). Looked for the button being drawn on the primary alone: projectManagerRows draws it for any GM with mapHidden (projects-ui.mjs:395), and openProjectManager is any GM's (684-687). The overlap itself was not measured; the road is read, and the E36-T10 class it reopens is recorded at projects-map.mjs:57-67.
